mission.title: Install and Configure Linode Kubernetes Engine (LKE)
mission.description: Linode Kubernetes Engine (LKE) is a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies the deployment and management of Kubernetes clusters on Linode's infrastructure. It is ideal for users looking for a hassle-free Kubernetes experience with integrated cloud services. Key trade-offs include limited customization compared to self-managed clusters and potential costs associated with cloud resources.

steps.title: Install the Linode CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the Linode CLI, which is necessary for managing Linode resources from the command line.

```bash

curl -sL https://github.com/linode/linode-cli/releases/download/v2.0.0/linode-cli-2.0.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -C /usr/local/bin

chmod +x /usr/local/bin/linode-cli

```

> This command downloads and extracts the Linode CLI to /usr/local/bin.
> Make the CLI executable.

steps.title: Create a Kubernetes Cluster
steps.description:
This command creates a new Kubernetes cluster with the specified version, node count, and region.

```bash

linode-cli k8s cluster-create --label my-k8s-cluster --region us-east --k8s-version 1.30 --node-count 3

```

> Replace 'my-k8s-cluster' with your desired cluster name.

steps.title: Set Up Kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures your kubeconfig file to connect to the newly created Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

linode-cli k8s kubeconfig-view my-k8s-cluster --text > ~/.kube/config

```

> This command saves the kubeconfig to your local machine.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This command checks the status of the nodes in your Kubernetes cluster to ensure they are running.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> You should see the nodes listed with a status of 'Ready'.

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
This step involves setting up autoscaling and monitoring for your cluster.

```bash

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/master/cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/linode/examples/cluster-autoscaler.yaml

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/monitoring/main/monitoring.yaml

```

> This command deploys the cluster autoscaler.
> This command sets up monitoring for your cluster.

uninstall.title: Delete the Kubernetes Cluster
uninstall.description:
This command will delete the Kubernetes cluster and all associated resources, which may result in data loss.

```bash

linode-cli k8s cluster-delete my-k8s-cluster

```

> Ensure you have backups of any important data before running this command.

uninstall.title: Remove the Linode CLI
uninstall.description:
This command removes the Linode CLI from your system.

```bash

rm /usr/local/bin/linode-cli

```

> This command deletes the Linode CLI binary.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the Kubernetes Cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up your data and check for any deprecated features.

```bash

kubectl get nodes -o wide

linode-cli k8s cluster-update my-k8s-cluster --k8s-version 1.30

kubectl get nodes

```

> Check the current status of your nodes.
> This command upgrades your cluster to the specified version.
> Verify that the nodes are back online and ready after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates an issue with the kubeconfig file or cluster certificate.

**Fix:**
Regenerate the kubeconfig file using 'linode-cli k8s kubeconfig-view my-k8s-cluster --text > ~/.kube/config'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'No resources found in kube-system namespace'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may occur if the Kubernetes cluster is not properly initialized.

**Fix:**
Ensure the cluster is created successfully and check the status with 'linode-cli k8s cluster-list'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient CPU resources'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the nodes do not have enough resources to schedule new pods.

**Fix:**
Scale up your cluster by adding more nodes using 'linode-cli k8s cluster-update my-k8s-cluster --node-count <new-count>'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to pull image'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may happen if the image is not available or the credentials are incorrect.

**Fix:**
Check the image name and ensure that the image is accessible from the cluster.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for new node types and improved integration with Linode's networking features.
versionNotes.deprecations: Deprecated the use of legacy API endpoints for cluster management.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: If upgrading from v1.29, ensure to update any scripts that reference deprecated endpoints.

resolution.summary: You should see a list of nodes with 'Ready' status when running 'kubectl get nodes'.
